title: Bollywood Romance 'Weekend' Eyes First Indian Feature Shoot in Russia's Yakutia
excerpt: Producer Vivek Singhania's Picture Perfect has signed a three-way MoU with Saidam Baryl and Sakhafilm, Yakutia's state-backed studio, to explore shooting the romantic drama in the Sakha Republic — a first for an Indian feature.
body:
• The Bollywood romantic drama Weekend is eyeing a shoot in Russia's Sakha Republic, known as Yakutia, after producer Vivek Singhania's Picture Perfect signed a memorandum of understanding with local outfits Saidam Baryl and Sakhafilm.
  • The three-way MoU, signed during the recently concluded 9th Yakutsk International Film Festival, is to explore taking the production to the region — it would be the first Indian feature film shoot in Yakutia.
  • Yakutia, in Russia's far east, has its own state-backed studio in Sakhafilm and a local industry nicknamed "Sakhawood," built despite winters that plunge below -40°C.
  • No cast, shooting schedule, or release plans for Weekend have been announced; the MoU covers exploration of the shoot, not a confirmed production start.

A Bollywood love story may soon be filmed in one of the coldest inhabited places on Earth. The Hindi-language romantic drama Weekend is eyeing a shoot in Russia's remote Sakha Republic, also known as Yakutia, after producer Vivek Singhania's banner Picture Perfect signed a memorandum of understanding with local outfits Saidam Baryl and Sakhafilm to explore taking the production there, Variety reported. The three-way MoU was signed during the recently concluded 9th Yakutsk International Film Festival.

A First for Indian Cinema

If the plan goes ahead, Weekend would be the first Indian feature film to shoot in Yakutia. Indian productions have filmed in Russia before, but not in the far-eastern republic, a vast territory of tundra and taiga centred on the city of Yakutsk. For Picture Perfect, the MoU is a first step: it commits the three companies to explore the production, rather than announcing a start date.

Sakhawood: The Industry at the Other End

The local partner brings an industry of its own. Yakutia has built a fiercely independent film sector — locals call it "Sakhawood," after the republic's other name, Sakha — telling stories of the region's indigenous people in the Yakut language. Its state-backed production company, Sakhafilm, came into being after the fall of communism in 1992 and specialises in shoots that would defeat most productions: camera crews there have worked in temperatures past -50°C, according to the New East Digital Archive's account of the industry. Bollywood is not a stranger in Yakutia, either: the archive recalls how, in the Soviet era, villagers across the region escaped into imported Indian films at village clubs, even as temperatures outside dropped below -40°C.

What Is Known — and What Is Not

Variety's report names the producer and the partners but no cast, director, or dates, and neither a shooting schedule nor release plans have been announced. What the agreement does signal is intent on both sides: an Indian banner looking for a landscape no Bollywood romance has used, and a regional industry that has spent three decades building the crews and infrastructure to host it. Whether Weekend's Yakutia shoot proceeds now depends on the exploration the MoU sets in motion.
